subject: Tailwind Health — performance qualification & dedicated GPU comparison
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Jordan <alex.jordan@tailwindhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-10T17:23:00Z
Subject: Tailwind Health — call recap & ask: latency / throughput targets

Alex — great to meet you and Jordan on the call earlier. Short recap and our asks so we can size a dedicated pilot that validates the SLOs we discussed.

Key targets you confirmed on the call:
- P95 generation latency (end-to-end, streaming enabled): <= 180 ms for 256-token responses (interactive chat)
- Sustained throughput target: 120 requests/sec (avg payload ~150 tokens) with expected peak bursts to 420 req/sec for short windows
- Concurrency target: ~30 concurrent sessions with KV caching and prefix reuse
- Streaming: chunked token-by-token streaming with max time-to-first-token target of 60 ms
- Data residency: US-only (private VPC option under procurement)

Proposed pilot baseline (what we suggest running):
- Two pilot node options to validate: H100 x4 (low-latency config) vs A100 80GB x6 (cost-optimized)
- Reserved throughput lanes: configure for 150 req/sec guaranteed, with autoscale/burst to 420 for short windows
- Test plan attachments: tailwind_throughput_matrix.xlsx (contains load profiles we sketched) and a short runbook PDF

Asks from your side to finalize pilot scope:
1) A short sample set (300 prompts) representing the mix of short/long chats and expected avg token length
2) Security contact to loop in for the Private deployment / compliance discussion (Jordan — I think you mentioned a security lead?)
3) Approval to provision a temporary dedicated pool for a 2-week validation window starting the week of Nov 29

Next steps:
- If you confirm the sample set + security contact, we’ll schedule a 30-min pilot kickoff and share our load harness and test script.
- Karthik/Sean: can you confirm feasibility of the two pilot node options and any immediate red flags?

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0142

1) Targets: the 180 ms P95 sounds right for interactive chat. We may also want to gate a stricter 120 ms P99 for a small subset of flows (triage UI). Can the pilot capture both?
2) Sample set: I’ll pull 350 example prompts (mix of short triage questions, longer multi-sentence clinical notes) and share by EOD Wednesday (Nov 17).
3) Security: looping in Jordan Lee (cc’d) — Jordan, can you confirm if Tailwind prefers VPC + customer-managed KMS for pilot?
4) Cost question: the H100 option looks attractive for latency, but what is the delta in-monthly cost vs A100? We’ll need a rough order-of-magnitude before we commit to node-heavy pilot.

Appreciate the clear next steps — excited to proceed.

Karthik / Sean — forwarding Alex’s reply. Two asks from me: (A) a quick feasibility note on pilot sizing and preferred GPU option for the SLOs (H100 x4 vs A100 x6) and (B) a short cost delta estimate to share with Alex.

Quick context: target 120 req/sec sustained, peaks to 420 req/sec, P95 <= 180 ms for 256 tokens; P99 120 ms for a small critical flow if we can capture it. Streaming with time-to-first-token <= 60 ms. Tailwind wants private (VPC) but will sign pilot NDA and we can run the pilot in our dedicated cluster isolated to their tenancy.

Proposed pilot acceptance criteria (what Tailwind will consider a pass):
- P95 <= 180 ms for interactive flows under sustained load for 30 minutes
- Systems hold 120 req/sec sustained with errors < 0.5% and CPU/GPU headroom for burst to 420 req/sec
- Streaming TTF < 60 ms for 90% of requests

Thanks — need a short note I can send back to Alex and Jordan by EOD so they can decide on provisioning.

— Ben

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Alex Jordan <alex.jordan@tailwindhealth.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@tailwindhealth.com>
Date: 2027-11-12T02:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Tailwind Health — call recap & ask: latency / throughput targets

Ben — high level feasibility & recommendation below. Sean and I discussed offline and sketched a short test plan.

Technical recommendation (pilot sizing):
- H100 x4 (low-latency opt) as primary pilot: this config gives best single-request latency with room for concurrency. Expect P95 ~120–160 ms for 256-token avg with continuous batching and KV cache exploited.
- A100 80GB x6 as a cost-optimized alternate: higher throughput for batched workloads but P95 likely ~170–230 ms depending on batch size and streaming chunking.
- If Tailwind prioritizes price + throughput over lowest tail latency, use A100 shortlist; if they require strict interactive latency (esp. that P99 120 ms flow), H100 is needed and we may need custom kernel tuning / eager kv cache warmup.

Reserved throughput sizing (config guidance):
- Reserve for 150 req/sec guaranteed (buffers to their 120 req/sec sustained ask). Configure burst window for 5 minutes to 420 req/sec using autoscale tokens.
- Concurrency: set conservative soft limit of 40 parallel inference contexts per pool node; expected utilization with KV reuse ~60–70% in steady state.

Streaming & batching knobs:
- Set micro-batch timeout ~6–10 ms to prioritize latency over large batch efficiency.
- Use token streaming with 64-token chunking for long responses to hit TTF targets; tune chunk-size post pilot.

Cost delta (very rough):
- Pilot H100 x4 (2-week reserved pilot): infra approx $28k–$38k (includes reserved capacity + engineer time + observability retention at pilot scale).
- Pilot A100 x6 (2-week): infra approx $20k–$28k.
Exact pricing depends on region and whether Tailwind signs a short reserved pilot commit. I’ll produce a concise estimate sheet if helpful.

Test plan (we’ll provide scripts):
1) Synthetic mixed load (350 prompts) run across 3 phases: ramp (10m), sustained (30m), burst (5m)
2) Measure P50/P95/P99 latencies, TTF for streaming, error rate, and GPU utilization per node
3) Capture KV cache hit-rate and effectiveness with prefix reuse
4) Run a small subset of real sample prompts to validate semantic parity across model variants

Attachments: test_script.sh (simple harness + curl wrapper), we’ll share observability dashboard links during the pilot.

If Alex/Jordan are comfortable we can schedule provisioning and kickoff the week of Nov 29. I’ll follow up with a short pilot-run cost worksheet if Ben wants to include it in the reply.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
